text:
Morgan Geekie has 20 points in 23 games for Boston, and on paper it's a strange mix: the goals are behind and the assists are ahead. He has five goals on 7.2 expected, so the finishing has been cold, but the Bruins have scored 6.8 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which is padding the helpers. Both of those tend to even out, in opposite directions.

He's playing 16.6 minutes a night and has dipped to 15.9 over his last ten, though nine of his points have come on the power play. Goalies have had his number on the best looks, including a Darcy Kuemper stop on a Geekie penalty shot in the Kings game.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was the same theme: 3.5 expected wins against 1.6 actual, chances that didn't convert. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of 1.6 royal-road or behind-the-net passes per 60. Watch the goal column. If the looks keep coming, the goals should start landing.
